questions.question: What is ServiceNow and what business problem does it solve?
options: A cloud-based platform for IT Service Management (ITSM) and business process automation — connects people, functions, and systems across an enterprise. Core: digitize workflows, replace manual/email-based processes, provide self-service, and track service delivery
questions.explanation: ServiceNow: cloud platform of record for enterprise service management. Originally ITSM (IT Help Desk), now spans: ITOM, HR, Customer Service, Legal, Security Operations, App Engine (custom apps). Single system of record — all departments use same platform, reducing silos.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow instance and what environments are typical?
options: A separate, isolated ServiceNow deployment with its own database and configuration — organizations typically have: Development (customize/test), Test/UAT (user acceptance), Production (live). ServiceNow recommends this 3-instance strategy. Each instance has its own URL (company.dev.service-now.com)
questions.explanation: Instance strategy: Dev (build and test), Test (QA/UAT), Prod (production). Change management: promote from Dev→Test→Prod via update sets. Cloning: periodically refresh Dev/Test with production data/config. Each instance: separate database, separate URL, separate admin credentials.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow Application Navigator?
options: The left-side navigation panel in ServiceNow UI — organizes all applications, modules, and records into a hierarchical tree. Use the search bar at top to quickly find any module. Favorites: star frequently used items. Recently visited items tracked automatically
questions.explanation: Application Navigator: left panel, filter by typing application name. All Applications: browse all installed apps. Modules: sub-items within each application. Filter navigator: type to search all modules/apps. Favorites: drag-to-add star icon. Recent items: quickly return to recently opened records.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow table and how does it relate to records?
options: Tables are the fundamental data structure — each table stores records of a specific type. Incident table: stores all incident records. Each row = one record, each column = one field. Tables can extend other tables (inheritance). sys_db_object: stores table definitions
questions.explanation: Tables: every application uses tables. Incident table [incident], Change Request [change_request], User [sys_user]. Table hierarchy: Task [task] is parent of Incident, Change, Problem, Service Request — they inherit task fields. sys_id: unique identifier on every record. Tables managed in System Definition > Tables.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Update Set and why is it important?
options: A container for capturing configuration changes made in one instance so they can be transported to another instance — essential for promoting changes from Development to Test to Production without manual re-configuration
questions.explanation: Update sets: capture: business rules, UI policies, client scripts, workflows, forms, lists, dictionary changes. NOT captured: data records (incidents, users), security permissions on fields, some system properties. Export → XML file → Import to target. Best practice: one update set per feature/change. Batch update sets: multiple updates in sequence.

questions.question: What are the main roles in ServiceNow and how is role-based access control (RBAC) configured?
options: Roles control what users can access and do — admin (full access), itil (IT staff — create/update tickets), approver_user (approve requests). Assign to users directly or via groups. Roles can contain other roles. Check: right-click field for Security → shows required roles
questions.explanation: Roles: defined in sys_user_role table. Users inherit roles from groups. itil: can read/write incidents, changes. sn_incident_write: more specific. Role check: sys_security_acl table. Best practice: assign roles via groups (not directly to users). Impersonate: admin impersonates user to test access.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Business Rule?
options: Server-side JavaScript that runs when records are displayed, inserted, updated, deleted, or queried — executes on the server. Uses: auto-populate fields, enforce business logic, call integration APIs. Conditions: when to run (before/after insert/update/delete)
questions.explanation: Business Rules: run on server. Timing: before (modify record before save), after (run after save, can send notifications), async (background, high-performance operations), display (populate variables for form). Current object: current.field. Previous values: previous.field. GlideRecord: query/modify other records.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Client Script?
options: JavaScript that runs in the user's browser — manipulates form fields, shows/hides sections, validates input before save. Types: onLoad (page loads), onChange (field changes), onSubmit (before form submit), onCellEdit (list edit). Cannot access server data directly (use GlideAjax)
questions.explanation: Client scripts: browser-side JavaScript. g_form API: manipulate form. g_form.setValue('priority', '2'). g_form.setVisible('field', false). g_form.setMandatory('field', true). onLoad: populate fields at load. onChange: react to field changes. Limitation: no direct database access — use GlideAjax (server call) for data lookups.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow UI Policy?
options: Declarative (no-code) rules for controlling form behavior based on conditions — make fields mandatory, read-only, or hidden when certain conditions are met. Runs client-side. Similar to Client Scripts but configuration-driven (no JavaScript required)
questions.explanation: UI Policies: if Priority = 'Critical' → make 'Assignment Group' mandatory and 'Workaround' visible. Actions: mandatory, read-only, visible. Condition: evaluated when form loads or condition field changes. Trigger on: specific field change or any change. Client Scripts: more complex logic. UI Policy: simpler, no-code, recommended for basic field behavior.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Workflow vs Flow Designer?
options: Workflow: older visual drag-and-drop workflow engine using activities (approvals, notifications, scripts, conditions). Flow Designer (modern): low-code, action-based, easier to build complex processes. ServiceNow migrating from Workflow to Flow Designer — recommended for new developments
questions.explanation: Workflow: classic engine, still used in legacy deployments. Flow Designer: modern low-code, uses triggers (record created/updated, schedule), actions (create record, ask for approval, send email, REST call, scripts). Subflows: reusable process blocks. Flow Designer integrations: Integration Hub spokes for external systems.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow SLA (Service Level Agreement)?
options: A time-based commitment for resolving or responding to tickets — configured as SLA Definition: conditions (which tickets it applies to), schedule (business hours), duration (target time), breach notifications. Visualized as percentage complete on ticket
questions.explanation: SLA in ServiceNow: Task SLA table attached to tickets. Timer: starts when condition met, pauses on 'on hold', stops when resolved. Metrics: Response SLA (first response), Resolution SLA (full resolution). Breach alerts: notification when 50%, 75%, 100% elapsed. Reports: SLA compliance rates. Business schedule: excludes weekends/holidays.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Notification?
options: Automated email, SMS, or push notification sent based on conditions — trigger: when/update or field change + condition. Recipients: users/groups. Template: subject + body with ${field} placeholders. Can use HTML. Subscriptions: users can opt in/out
questions.explanation: Notifications: System Notification > Notifications. When to send: record inserted/updated + condition. Recipients: field values (Assigned to, Caller), user lists, groups. Message template: ${caller_id.name}, ${number}, ${short_description}. Email digest: group notifications. Device: email (most common), SMS, push. MID Server: required for some delivery methods.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow CMDB (Configuration Management Database)?
options: A repository of all IT configuration items (CIs) and their relationships — servers, applications, databases, services and how they interconnect. Basis for ITSM processes: incidents linked to affected CIs, changes impact analyzed via CI relationships
questions.explanation: CMDB: Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] base table. CI classes: Server, Application, Database, Network Device. Relationships: depends on, hosted on, connects to. Populated by: Discovery (auto-scan), SCCM integration, manual entry. CMDB Health: duplicate detection, completeness scoring. CI relations: used in change impact analysis, incident correlation.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow Discovery?
options: Automated process that scans networks to find and populate CI data in the CMDB — uses MID Server to probe devices via SNMP, WMI, SSH, and other protocols. Discovers: servers, network devices, applications, databases, cloud resources
questions.explanation: Discovery: sets up IP ranges, credentials (SSH, WinRM, SNMP, cloud API), and MID Servers. Probes: horizontal discovery (find IPs) → vertical discovery (classify + attribute collection). Creates/updates CMDB CIs. Schedule: daily/weekly. Discovery Schedules: System Definition > Scheduler. Requires: Discovery plugin + MID Server in network.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow MID Server?
options: A Java application deployed on-premises that acts as a secure communication channel between ServiceNow cloud instance and internal network — enables Discovery, integrations, orchestration for on-prem resources without opening inbound firewall ports
questions.explanation: MID Server: installed on Windows/Linux VM inside corporate network. Outbound HTTPS only to ServiceNow — no inbound ports needed. Functions: Discovery (scan internal network), JDBC probes (database queries), SNMP, WMI, SSH, REST/SOAP integrations, Orchestration activities. High availability: multiple MID servers with ECC queue load balancing.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Access Control List (ACL)?
options: Record-level and field-level security rules that determine what operations (read, write, create, delete) different roles can perform on specific tables or fields — more granular than roles alone
questions.explanation: ACLs: table.operation (incident.read, incident.write). Evaluated: does user's role match? Additional script condition? Field-level: incident.caller_id.read — restrict who can see caller field. Types: table (row-level), field (column-level), UI action (buttons). Right-click field for Security shortcut. Evaluated: top-down, first match wins.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Scheduled Job?
options: Automates tasks that run on a defined schedule — daily data cleanup, reports generation, data imports, system maintenance. Uses GlideRecord scripts. Types: Script (custom JS), Report delivery, Import set, Transform map execution
questions.explanation: Scheduled Jobs: System Definition > Scheduled Jobs. Specify: run time (specific date, daily, weekly, monthly, periodically), time zone, active. Script: GlideRecord queries, API calls, calculations. Common uses: purge old records, update aggregate tables, daily email summaries, SLA recalculations. sys_trigger table.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Transform Map?
options: Maps fields from imported data (Import Set) to target table fields — defines how incoming data translates to ServiceNow records. Can include transform scripts for data manipulation. After import: run transform to create/update records in target table
questions.explanation: Data import flow: external file/API → Import Set table (raw data staging) → Transform Map (field mappings + coalesce fields for matching) → Target table (create/update records). Coalesce: if existing record with matching field exists, update it (prevent duplicates). Transform scripts: manipulate values during transform.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow Service Catalog?
options: Self-service portal where users can request services and products — IT requests (new laptop, VPN access), HR requests (onboarding), facilities requests. Items use catalog item forms to collect information, Flow Designer for fulfillment
questions.explanation: Service Catalog: catalog items (RITM generated), record producers (create records directly), order guides (multi-item requests). Variables: information collected at request time. Approval workflow: auto-triggered. Fulfillment: Flow Designer or Workflow. Service Portal: modern UI for employee self-service. Catalog categories: organize items.

questions.question: What is the difference between an Incident and a Service Request in ServiceNow?
options: Incident: unexpected interruption or degradation of IT service — restore service ASAP (reactive). Service Request (RITM): request for a new service, information, or standard change — fulfill a need (proactive). Different SLAs, different workflows, different tables
questions.explanation: Incident: unplanned event, goal = restore service (break/fix). RITM (Requested Item): planned fulfillment, goal = deliver requested item/service. Change: controlled modification to environment. Problem: root cause investigation of recurring incidents. Each has own table, SLAs, workflows, and KPIs.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Reference Field and why is it important?
options: A field that stores a reference (sys_id) to a record in another table — displays the display value but stores the sys_id. Example: Assigned to field references sys_user table. Dot-walking: assigned_to.email navigates to referenced record's field
questions.explanation: Reference fields: store sys_id, display label (display value). Dot-walking: script access to referenced fields (current.assigned_to.email). GlideRecord: gr.assigned_to.getDisplayValue(). In reports: can access referenced table fields using dot-walk. Reference qualifiers: filter what values appear in dropdown.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow Orchestration?
options: Automates tasks on remote systems without human intervention — run scripts on servers (via MID Server), configure network devices, provision VMs. Activities: PowerShell, SSH, JDBC, REST. Triggered by Change Management, Incidents, or scheduled
questions.explanation: Orchestration: requires Orchestration plugin + MID Server. Activities: SSH command, PowerShell script, JDBC query, REST call. Activity Designer: build custom activities. Triggers: from workflows/flows or manual. Common uses: auto-provision accounts, configure servers from changes, remediate incidents automatically. Runbook Automation.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow Global domain vs a custom domain?
options: Domain separation: segregates data between different organizational units (departments, subsidiaries, customers) within one ServiceNow instance — each domain sees only their records. Global domain: default, seen by all. MSP use case: each customer = their own domain
questions.explanation: Domain separation: Enterprise feature. Creates hierarchical data visibility. MSP/outsourcer: multiple customers in one instance, each sees only their data. TOP domain: global. Sub-domains: customer1, customer2. Users: assigned to domain, see only domain records. Admin: can switch domain context. More complex than separate instances.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow UI Action?
options: A button, menu item, or link on a form or list that triggers a script when clicked — can run client-side or server-side scripts. Examples: 'Resolve' button on incident (changes state, sets resolved fields), 'Request Approval' button
questions.explanation: UI Actions: appear as form buttons, related links, or context menu items. Condition: when to show (show Resolve button only when state is 'In Progress'). Script: GlideRecord operations, state changes, notifications. Client script: checkbox = runs JavaScript in browser. onclick: additional browser-side code. Table/global scope.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow Performance Analytics?
options: Add-on for tracking KPIs and metrics over time — define indicators (metrics calculated from table data), collect data points on a schedule, visualize trends on dashboards. Use for: SLA compliance trends, incident volume over time, backlog analysis
questions.explanation: Performance Analytics: indicators (defined formulas against table data), collector jobs (run daily/weekly to store snapshots), widgets (line charts, column charts, scorecard). Dashboards: combine multiple widgets. Breakdowns: analyze by category, assignment group, priority. Essential for service reporting and continual improvement.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Import Set?
options: A staging table for importing data from external sources — data lands in import_set_row table first (raw), then transform maps move data to target tables. Sources: Excel, CSV, JDBC, REST API, SFTP. Allows data validation before committing to live tables
questions.explanation: Import set flow: source (file/API) → Import Set table (raw staging with all data as strings) → Transform Map (map columns, scripts, coalesce) → Target table (Incidents, Users, CIs, etc.). Benefits: staging allows review before transform, error handling, rerun. Load time: schedule or on-demand.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Gauge/Dashboard?
options: Interactive homepage where users see live data visualizations — gauges, charts, reports, activity feeds. Personal homepages or shared departmental dashboards. Drag-and-drop layout. Admin creates default homepage for roles, users customize their own
questions.explanation: Dashboards: System UI > Homepages or Analytics Center. Add: widgets (reports, gauges, activity streams, clocks). Gauges: semi-circle showing current value vs target. Column/Pie/Bar charts from saved reports. Share: with role, group, or everyone. Auto-refresh: configurable interval. Mobile: available in ServiceNow mobile app.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow Service Portal vs Classic UI?
options: Service Portal: modern responsive web interface (widget-based, AngularJS) for end-users and approvers — self-service, cleaner consumer-style UX. Classic UI (UI16): traditional desktop interface for IT staff managing records and configuration. Both access same data
questions.explanation: Service Portal (sp): end-user facing, mobile-friendly, customizable with widgets. Developers create custom portals and pages. Classic UI: IT operations — form view, list view, administration. Platform UI (Polaris/Next Experience in Tokyo+): newer unified interface. Most orgs: Service Portal for employees, Classic/Polaris for IT staff.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Application Scope?
options: Namespace that isolates customizations and code from other applications — prevents naming conflicts, controls which tables/scripts can access which. Global scope: accessible everywhere. Scoped apps: isolated, must explicitly share. Best practice: develop in scoped applications
questions.explanation: Scopes: each application has a scope prefix (x_company_appname). Scoped app scripts: only access own tables (unless shared). Global scope: all scripts see global scope. Custom applications: always create in scoped application (prevents future upgrade conflicts). Scoped apps: can be published to App Store.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow ITIL process alignment?
options: ServiceNow is built around ITIL best practices — Incident Management, Problem Management, Change Management, Service Level Management, Service Catalog, CMDB, Event Management, Knowledge Management are all ITIL processes implemented as ServiceNow applications
questions.explanation: ITIL v4 alignment: Service Desk (Incidents), Problem (root cause), Change (CAB, normal/standard/emergency), Configuration (CMDB), Release, Service Catalog, Knowledge, Service Level, Event Management. ServiceNow certified ITIL process workflows. CSA exam: understand ITIL concepts applied in ServiceNow context.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Knowledge Base?
options: A repository of articles that help users resolve issues through self-service or guide agents — Knowledge Base → Categories → Articles. Published articles appear in Service Portal for self-service. Article feedback: helpful/not helpful ratings. Integration: suggest articles during incident creation
questions.explanation: Knowledge: System Knowledge > Knowledge. Knowledge Bases (KBs): separate repos (IT, HR, Facilities). Categories: organize articles. Workflow: draft → review → published. Search: full-text in Service Portal and Classic UI. Metrics: views, usefulness ratings. Auto-suggest: incident form suggests articles based on short description.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow IntegrationHub?
options: Extends Flow Designer with pre-built integration spokes for external systems — spokes: Jira, Slack, GitHub, Salesforce, AWS, ServiceNow-to-ServiceNow. Each spoke: ready-to-use actions for common operations (create Jira issue, send Slack message, create AWS instance)
questions.explanation: IntegrationHub: subscription-based. Spokes: ~150+ including Jira, GitHub, Slack, Teams, Salesforce, AWS, Azure, GCP, Office 365. Each spoke: set of actions (create/update/delete/query). Flow Designer: drag-and-drop integration in 15 minutes. Custom spokes: build your own using REST/SOAP/JDBC actions. Replaces complex scripted integrations.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Catalog Variable Set?
options: Reusable groups of catalog variables that can be added to multiple catalog items — instead of re-creating the same fields (department, location, justification) in every catalog item, create a variable set and include it in all items
questions.explanation: Variable sets: create once (department, business justification, manager name), add to 10+ catalog items. Changes: update variable set → all catalog items updated. Variable types: Single line text, multi-line, checkbox, reference, lookup select. Variable rules: show/hide variables based on other variable values.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow Agent Workspace?
options: A modern, unified interface for IT agents handling incidents, requests, and cases — configurable workspace with: multi-tab browsing, context panels, omni-channel (email, chat, voice), guided setup, quick actions. Replaces classic form view for support agents
questions.explanation: Agent Workspace: workspace.service-now.com. Features: multiple record tabs open simultaneously, context panel (related records, CI info), incoming work queues, collaboration, omni-channel (email/chat/voice in same view). Custom configurations: which panels, quick actions, views. Improves agent productivity vs classic UI.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Process Flow Formatter?
options: A visual status tracker on forms showing the progression through workflow stages — displays colored blocks for each stage (New → In Progress → Resolved → Closed). Clicking a stage can trigger state change. Gives agents and users a clear view of where a record is in its lifecycle
questions.explanation: Process flow formatter: added to form layout as a formatter element. Defines states shown as blocks. Current state highlighted. Configuration: which states display, allow clicking to advance state. Common on: Incident form (New/In Progress/On Hold/Resolved/Closed), Change form (Draft/Assess/Authorize/Scheduled/Implement/Review/Closed).

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow GlideRecord and when is it used?
options: The primary server-side API for querying and manipulating ServiceNow database tables in scripts — used in Business Rules, Script Includes, Scheduled Jobs. var gr = new GlideRecord('incident'); gr.addQuery('state', 1); gr.query(); while(gr.next()) { ... }
questions.explanation: GlideRecord: CRUD operations on tables. addQuery: filter records. query(): execute. next(): iterate results. getValue/setValue: field values. insert(): create record. update(): save changes. deleteRecord(): delete. Limit results: setLimit(100). Order: orderBy/orderByDesc. Script Includes: reusable GlideRecord functions called by other scripts.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow sys_id field?
options: A globally unique 32-character hexadecimal identifier assigned to every record in ServiceNow — immutable, used as foreign key in reference fields, referenced in URLs. Never changes. sys_id is the true identifier, display values can change
questions.explanation: sys_id: format is 32 hex chars (e.g., 9d385017c611228701d22104cc95c371). Every table, every record has one. URL: incident.do?sys_id=ABC123. Reference fields: store sys_id, display label separately. Scripts: gr.sys_id.toString(). New records: generated automatically (UUID). Not visible in standard UI but accessible in field info.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow Now Platform's Configuration vs Customization?
options: Configuration: using built-in ServiceNow features (UI policies, business rules, workflows) without modifying core code — upgradeable and supported. Customization: modifying ServiceNow baseline scripts/forms in global scope — may break on upgrades. Best practice: configure, don't customize
questions.explanation: ServiceNow upgrade path: configurations in scoped apps or update sets survive upgrades. Customizations to global scope scripts: may be overwritten on upgrade. Rule: if you can achieve the goal with configuration (UI Policy, Business Rule, Flow) without touching baseline records, do that. Scoped applications: safest custom development approach.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow Event Management?
options: Correlates and processes events from monitoring tools (SNMP traps, syslog, API events) and creates alerts and incidents automatically — reduces noise by correlating related events, suppressing duplicates, and creating actionable alerts. Closes alerts when events resolve
questions.explanation: Event Management: events → rules (dedup, correlation, CI lookup) → alerts → incident creation. Event sources: Nagios, Zabbix, SCOM, cloud watchdog. CI enrichment: lookup CI in CMDB from event hostname/IP. Alert suppression: if CI in maintenance mode. AIOps: ML-based anomaly detection and correlation (requires subscription).

questions.question: What is the difference between a ServiceNow Standard Change and Normal Change?
options: Standard Change: pre-approved, low-risk, routine procedure (e.g., apply monthly patches) — no individual CAB approval needed, uses a template. Normal Change: requires full review and CAB (Change Advisory Board) approval — for non-routine changes with moderate-to-high risk
questions.explanation: Change types: Standard (pre-approved, template-based, no CAB), Normal (full CAB review, risk assessment), Emergency (expedited approval for urgent changes). Change workflow: Draft → Assess → Authorize → Scheduled → Implement → Review → Closed. CAB (Change Advisory Board): group that reviews normal changes.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow's Virtual Agent?
options: Conversational AI chatbot platform — employees interact via natural language. Automated conversations handle common requests (reset password, check request status, submit incidents) without human agent. Topics: pre-built conversation flows. Integrates with Teams, Slack, SMS, web chat
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent: NLU (Natural Language Understanding) understands intent. Topics: conversation flows (pre-built for common ITSM tasks + custom). Can: create incidents, request items, check status, answer KB questions, route to live agent. Channels: Service Portal, Microsoft Teams, Slack, web widget. Analytics: containment rate tracking.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow Predictive Intelligence?
options: AI/ML feature that automatically categorizes and routes incoming incidents and requests — trained on historical data to predict: category, priority, assignment group. Reduces manual triage. Also: similar incident suggestion, field recommendations
questions.explanation: Predictive Intelligence: trains ML models on historical ticket data. Predictions: category, subcategory, assignment group, priority. Auto-applies suggestions or requires agent confirmation. Similar incidents: shows related past incidents for faster resolution. Training: requires minimum 400 records per class. Monitors prediction accuracy over time.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow IntegrationHub ETL?
options: Extract, Transform, Load capability within IntegrationHub for syncing large datasets from external systems to ServiceNow — scheduled pulls, field mapping, transformation rules. More powerful than basic import sets for complex integrations
questions.explanation: IntegrationHub ETL (Enterprise): for large-scale data integrations. Configure: source (REST, JDBC, CSV), schedule, field mappings, transformations. Optimized for high volume. For most integrations: Integration Spoke + Flow Designer sufficient. ETL: when syncing large external datasets on schedule (HRIS, asset management, CMDB sources).

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Record Producer?
options: A catalog item that creates a record in any ServiceNow table (not just fulfillment) — when submitted, creates an Incident, Problem, Change, or any custom record. Provides a guided, user-friendly form for record creation instead of the technical native form
questions.explanation: Record Producers: Service Catalog item that maps submitted variables to table fields. Create incident via catalog: provides friendly form, maps 'Describe your issue' to short_description. No RITM created — directly creates target record. Used when: want catalog-style UX for creating any record type.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow's Configuration Item (CI) relationship and how is it used?
options: CIs have typed relationships: Depends on::Used by, Hosted on::Hosts, Connects to::Connected from, etc. Relationships power: change impact analysis (what's downstream?), incident correlation (same CI = related incidents), service maps (visual CI topology)
questions.explanation: CI Relationships: create in CMDB Relationships section. Visualization: Dependency Views, Service Maps. Change impact: select CI on change → see downstream CIs at risk. Service map: business service → apps → servers → infrastructure. Discovery automatically creates relationships. Used in Event Management: alert correlation for related CIs.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow Report Designer?
options: Tool for creating reports and charts from ServiceNow data — report types: list, bar chart, pie chart, trend, multi-level pivot, heatmap, calendar, funnel, score. Schedule: email to users. Add to dashboards. Share with roles/groups
questions.explanation: Report Designer: Reports > Create New. Data source: table or data source (pre-filtered table). Filter: conditions to limit records. Group by: aggregate data. Report type: bar, pie, trend, etc. Run report: see results. Schedule: send via email on schedule. Add to dashboard widget. Share: by role, group, or public.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow Approval process?
options: Structured approval workflow — approvals created for Catalog requests, Changes, Problems. Approvers: specific users, group (anyone in group), all in group. Actions: Approve, Reject, Request Info. Approval Rules: automatic approval based on conditions (low-cost requests auto-approve)
questions.explanation: Approvals: sc_approval (catalog) or sysapproval_approver (general). Flow Designer: Ask for Approval action. States: Requested, Approved, Rejected, Not yet requested, Duplicate. Multiple approvals: parallel (all must approve) or sequential (one at a time). Escalation: auto-approve after X days or notify manager.

questions.question: What is ServiceNow's Connection & Credential record?
options: Secure storage for integration credentials (API keys, usernames/passwords, OAuth tokens) used by IntegrationHub and Discovery — credentials stored encrypted, referenced by name in scripts/flows. Never hardcode credentials in scripts
questions.explanation: Connection & Credential aliases: define once, reference everywhere. Credential types: Basic (user/pass), API Key, OAuth 2.0, Certificate. Discovery: credentials for SSH, WMI, SNMP. IntegrationHub: API keys for external systems. Scripts: gs.getProperty or Connection API. Never paste credentials into scripts — use credential aliases.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow Upgrade process?
options: ServiceNow provides regular upgrades (family releases like Tokyo, Utah, Vancouver) — test in non-production first. Skipping customizations: ServiceNow flags conflicts between your customizations and baseline changes. Review/revert conflicts after upgrade. Use: Upgrade Center to manage process
questions.explanation: Upgrade process: (1) Notify/schedule upgrade in non-prod. (2) Run upgrade. (3) Review Upgrade Center for skipped customizations (conflicts). (4) Test thoroughly. (5) Upgrade production. Family releases: twice yearly (Tokyo, Utah, Vancouver, Washington...). Patch releases: monthly security/bug fixes. Scoped apps: less likely to conflict than global.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow Table Hierarchy and how does inheritance work?
options: Tables can extend other tables — child table inherits all parent fields. Task [task] is parent: Incident, Change, Problem, Service Request all inherit task fields (number, state, assigned to, priority). Polymorphic queries on parent table return all child records
questions.explanation: Table hierarchy: sys_db_object defines inheritance. Incident extends Task: all task fields available on incident form. Custom fields on Task: appear on all child tables. Query Task table: returns incidents + changes + problems. Parent-child: use sys_class_name field to distinguish. Extends list view: click Show Table Hierarchy in Studio.
